newsitem.title: USA: Lan Chile puts emphasis on cargo business.
newsitem.headline: Lan Chile puts emphasis on cargo business.

text.p: Lan Chile looks at its passenger aircraft as cargo planes with seats, a top Lan Chile official told a meeting of finance and airline executives Tuesday.
"We are a cargo airline that carries passengers," Jorge Castillo, leasing and insurance director Lan Chile Group, told the conference on Financing Commercial Aviation in the Americas.
Lan Chile executives believe "you must fill up every single cargo position you have got," Castillo said.
In fact, Lan sells its entire belly space to its all-cargo sister company Fast Air and Lan must "buy back" the space for passenger luggage, he said.

The cargo concentration extends to all decisions of the company. Castillo said Lan dropped a non-stop flight from Santiago to Madrid because the cargo business was not good enough. "We don't care about market share or national pride. We want to make money," he said.
Lan Chile's selection of aircraft is also driven by cargo. "The Boeing (Co ) 757 is not a good cargo aircraft, so we don't want it," he said.

About 30 percent of Lan Chile's revenues are from cargo, compared with about five percent for most U.S. passenger carriers. When sister company Fast Air is included, about 50 percent of the group's profits are from cargo, he said.
Lan Chile and Fast Air are both part of the Lan Chile Group. The group also includes LADECO.
